keyTerms.definition: The instructors of the CS229 foundations course.
Minimum sufficient explanation, strong answer, red flags, rubric, remediation.

recall.question: What is this file?
recall.answer: Keys for the unit U13 interview questions. Each answer gives the minimum sufficient explanation, a strong answer, common red flags, a rubric, and remediation.

keyTerms.definition: L_pre(theta) = (1/n) sum_i l_pre(x^(i), theta).
Broad pretraining, then adaptation to downstream tasks.

recall.question: B1: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: L_pre(theta) = (1/n) sum_i l_pre(x^(i), theta). Phases: pretraining on broad (usually unlabeled) data, then adaptation to downstream tasks.

keyTerms.definition: min_w (1/n_task) sum_i l_task(y^(i), w^T phi_theta-hat(x^(i))).
The backbone theta-hat; only the head w trains.

recall.question: B2: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: min_w (1/n_task) sum_i l_task(y^(i), w^T phi_theta-hat(x^(i))). The backbone theta-hat is frozen, only the head w trains.

keyTerms.definition: Delta W = B A; trainable count r(d_out + d_in).
alpha / r.

recall.question: B3: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: Delta W = B A, h = W_0 x + (alpha / r) B A x. Trainable count r(d_out + d_in).

keyTerms.definition: Two augmentations of the same image.
An augmentation of a different image.

recall.question: B4: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: positive pair = two augmentations of the same image. Negative (random) pair = an augmentation of a different image.

keyTerms.definition: -sum_i log(exp(pos_i) / (exp(pos_i) + sum_{j != i} exp(neg_{ij}))).
Growing a positive inner product lowers the loss.

recall.question: B5: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: L_pre = -sum_i log(exp(pos_i) / (exp(pos_i) + sum_{j != i} exp(neg_{ij}))). Growing a positive inner product lowers the loss.

keyTerms.definition: |R(q) intersect top-k| / |R(q)|.
DCG@k / IDCG@k with logarithmic discount.

recall.question: B6: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: Recall@k = |R(q) intersect top-k| / |R(q)|, NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k with logarithmic discount. Recall@k ignores ranking.

keyTerms.definition: The probe is convex quadratic; finetuning is nonconvex.

recall.question: What are the D1 answers?
recall.answer: D1.2: w = [1.0, 0.0], train MSE 0.0. D1.3: the probe is linear in w with squared loss (closed form); finetuning optimizes a nonconvex neural loss.

keyTerms.definition: Loss 3.3532, then 3.2695 after moving positives 10% closer.
Collapse: no pressure keeping embeddings apart.

recall.question: What are the D2 answers?
recall.answer: D2.2: loss 3.3532, after the 10% closer step, 3.2695. D2.4: collapse: the loss has no pressure keeping embeddings apart.

recall.question: Q1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: f = -log p + log(p + q). df/dp = -1/p + 1/(p+q) = -q/(p(p+q)) < 0. df/dq = 1/(p+q) > 0. Holds for p, q > 0.

keyTerms.definition: The denominator must sum j != i.
Divide each embedding by its norm first.

recall.question: T1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Bug 1: the denominator sums over all j including i; the notes' variant sums j != i. Bug 2: embeddings are not normalized. Check: moving each positive pair closer must lower the loss.

keyTerms.definition: HNSW, quantization, or inverted-file indexes.
Accept a small chance of missing the exact nearest neighbor.

recall.question: S1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Use an approximate nearest-neighbor index: HNSW graph search, quantization, or inverted-file/centroid indexes. Monitor index recall against brute force and tail latency.

keyTerms.definition: The image and its paired text.
The image with other items' texts.

recall.question: S2: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Positive pair: the image and its paired text (two views of one underlying item). Negative pairs: the image with other items' texts (and symmetrically).

keyTerms.definition: The 40 tasks are all near the pretraining distribution.
Sort tasks by shift, sweep rank r, find the boundary.

recall.question: R1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Hidden condition: the 40 tasks are all near the pretraining distribution, where a low-rank update has enough capacity. It fails under large shifts or high-rank changes.
